invariants: Every new or changed English string gets a Welsh draft beside it in the same change, as the service's other copy does.

Every changed page works fully without JavaScript: every state change is a form post, every search and filter a form with a button that submits it, and JavaScript only enhances a page that already works (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 6; conflicts:c-006).

A behaviour is built with GOV.UK Frontend first, then another tested government library (Ministry of Justice, HMRC, Scottish Government); no custom JavaScript is written to copy the prototype, pop-ups are not built and confirmations stay pages (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 5, 7 and 19).
Pages are built from GOV.UK Frontend components and govuk-* classes; the prototype's custom app-dr2-* blocks are not copied.

A search box is the real frontend's accessible autocomplete over a native select and behaves as the real frontend configures it; its entries are what MDM serves through reference-data, and only how the list reads follows the prototype (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 1 to 4).

Where a row changes a page or behaviour the high-risk plants frontend also has, the same increment changes plants too: plants mirrors the structure, wording patterns, components and behaviour, and keeps its own questions, data and step order (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claims 43 and 44).
Shared wording in a frontend's shared copy is never reworded in place; a set-specific string goes in the feature's own copy (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 41).

Notification statuses are only ever added, never renamed or removed, and each new status is mapped in every frontend that reads it before the animals backend first sends it (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm claim 42).
A page in its error state keeps the 'Error: ' prefix on its browser title (conflicts:c-006).
'Save and return to overview' saves without the page's required-answer checks, but still refuses an answer that fails its own format rule (conflicts:c-211; ruling:sam-2026-10-07).
Notifications, templates and address book entries stay scoped to the signed-in user's organisation (or user, for templates); nothing lists another organisation's records.
Each increment updates the tests repo's specs, page objects and journey helpers its change breaks, in the same change.

increments.title: A completed notification shows as complete with no Amend button
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 shows a finished notification as 'Submission complete' (or its own status text, such as 'Completed') and stops amendment. 'Completed' is added as a new status, never replacing one. No completed status reaches the real service today: post-submission outcomes would come from the authorities' case system, which sends none back yet.
acceptanceCriteria: A completed notification's view shows the status tag 'Submission complete', or its own status text such as 'Completed' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-022; prototype:dr2-1-specs prototype-dr2-1-specs-p5-103; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-099, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-100)

A completed notification's view header has no 'Amend this notification' button, and still offers 'Copy as new' as the primary button and 'Delete' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p11-026)

Every existing status (Draft, Submitted, Submitted action required) still shows as it did before 'Completed' was added (ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-070, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-071, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-072)

On a completed notification in the animals sets, 'Delete' removes it from the set's own list with the deletion banner, and the backend publishes a NotificationSubmissionDeleted event for it. (trace:prototype-dr2-1 trace-prototype-dr2-1-p14-013; repo:backend repo-backend-p3-034)

The likely one is the authorities' case system (PIMS Dynamics) sending post-submission outcomes back to the notification record (as req-1082). Who: the programme owner names and builds that source. Until then nothing here can be built or seen.

req-2114 waits on the same source: the authorities' case system (PIMS Dynamics) must send post-submission outcomes, including completed, back to the notification record (as req-1082). Who: the programme owner names and builds that source.
notes: Blocked: req-910 carries blockedBy on a real source of completion (9 October ruling, claim 99). Once unblocked, it lands after the rows 'A submitted notification's view has a header…' and 'View header offers Amend, Copy as new and Delete…', and alongside whatever row builds that source. 'Completed' is a new status added beside the others, never replacing one; whether plants follows is decided when it unblocks (afternoon ruling, claims p2-070, p2-071, p3-065 and p3-066).

req-2114 (cross-area pass) adds what a Completed notification can do: copy and delete, never amend. It waits on the same completion source as req-910, so it joins this blocked row rather than holding up the manage-notifications rows.

increments.title: Overview totals count only positive numbers
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1's Overview adds only positive counts to the Animals and Packages/boxes totals, so a card never shows a negative or odd total. Held until the reconciler says how such a count could reach the Overview.
acceptanceCriteria: On the Overview, the Animals and Packages/boxes totals add only the positive counts on each commodity line: a zero, negative or non-numeric count adds nothing, and a total that is not above zero reads '0' (prototype:dr2-1-source prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-014, prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-015; repo:frontend repo-frontend-p4-010)
openQuestions: Sent back to the reconciler: no trader can enter a zero, negative or non-numeric count (the commodity details page refuses any number of animals or packages below 1, and a template is seeded from the same checked answers), so the change cannot be observed in any environment. The reconciler decides whether req-787 is already met as far as anyone can observe, or names how such a count can reach the Overview.
notes: Drafted by the combiner: the notification-hub drafter listed req-787 as unobservable. It is held here, blocked on the reconciler's answer, so the buildable Overview rows are not held up.

Dropped: the reconciler adopted req-787 as already met (delta exists). Commodity details refuses a number of animals or packages below 1 or not whole, and templates are seeded from the same checked answers, so no zero, negative or non-numeric count can reach the Overview; blank counts already add nothing and both totals already read 0 before any line exists.

increments.title: A draft's review shows the view header with its Draft status and stays editable
increments.detail: Design Release 2.1 heads a draft's review the way it heads a submitted notification's view, and keeps it editable with what is still incomplete listed. The 9 October ruling keeps that content, keys the header on the real service's one review route and the stored status, and keeps dashboard draft rows going to the hub (c-246). Today a draft's review, reached from the hub's 'Review and submit', has the journey heading and the status strip and no header. Afterwards the same review, for a Draft, shows the view header drawn in the set's own template with the status strip off: the Draft tag, the reference as heading, the date created, Copy as new, Delete and the Import reference numbers, and stays editable. Plants' draft check answers takes the same header in the same increment, without Copy as new.
